submitted.rationale: Index 23 (Sb0.82Zn0.18) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0076%, about 5x index 29 and far above index 16. It lies near the Sb-rich ZnSb4O8/ZnSb4O9 compositions, which MEGNet predicts to have small gaps and so absorb 2.4 eV light. The GP also ranked it top.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE ~0 (-7.6e-5%). Near ZnSb2O6, a wide-gap trirutile that does not absorb at 2.4 eV.
Not measured. The Zn-rich region is dominated by wide-gap ZnO/spinel, and the measurements showed the Sb-rich trend was better.

consultations.verdict: Support (weak). MEGNet predicts ZnSb2O6 (mp-3188) at 1.97 eV HSE, which is below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it would absorb. Index 16 sits at the ZnSb2O6 stoichiometry (Sb 0.66). The model's predicted gaps are likely underestimated (the experimental gap is ~3.4 eV), so this is low-confidence. ZnSb2O4 (4.2 eV) would not absorb.

Support (weak). The Sb-rich phase ZnSb4O9 (mp-1041117) has a predicted gap near 0 eV, and Sb6O13 (1.97-2.05 eV) is mixed-valence. Both suggest visible absorption at the Sb-rich end. ZnSb2O6 at index 16 gave essentially zero EQE, so testing the opposite, Sb-rich extreme is the most informative next step.

Support (weak). MEGNet gives ZnSb4O8 (mp-1043668, Sb 0.8) a 0.48 eV gap, so it would absorb 2.4 eV light. Index 23 (Sb 0.82) is close to that composition. The GP also ranks index 23 top by UCB after index 29 (Sb-rich) beat index 16.
